The test image shows a corn ear with:
- Large white/gray gall structure at the top
- Dark black masses/spores throughout
- Orange/yellow kernels still visible

This is a pod/ear. Top candidates: Common_Smut (seed) and Head_Smut (pod). Let me check both.

The comparison is clear. The test image shows individual galls at various stages (white/silvery to black) growing among visible orange/yellow kernels on a corn ear — exactly matching Common Smut. All other ear rot diseases show fundamentally different patterns (colored molds, complete ear replacement, or powdery growth).

The Common_Smut seed reference (Corn_Disease_218.jpg) is a near-identical match: white-to-black galls interspersed among normal kernels on the same ear.

```json
{"prediction": "Common_Smut", "confidence": 0.93, "reasoning": "Test image shows a corn ear with individual galls at multiple maturity stages — white/silvery membrane at the top transitioning to dark black spore masses — growing among visible orange/yellow kernels. This is the defining pattern of Common Smut. Reference image Corn_Disease_218 (Common_Smut/seed) is a near-identical match. Head Smut replaces the entire ear with spore masses (no individual kernels visible), and all ear rot diseases (Diplodia, Gibberella, Trichoderma, Aspergillus) show colored mold growth rather than discrete galls."}
```
